lines.name: Dumbarton Cutoff trains, Redwood City to Niles
lines.summary: Southern Pacific trains from Redwood City across the Dumbarton bridge to Newark, Centerville and Niles, at first four trains a day to and from Niles, by 1914 one mixed train each way, daily except Sunday.
lines.fate_note: Passengers ended with the timetable of October 1, 1916; the cutoff carried only freight after that.

route.note: From Redwood City station, the trains ran about a mile down the main line to Redwood Junction, which isn't drawn as part of this line.

sources.note: The first regular passenger train, Tuesday, December 26, 1911; four trains a day between Niles and Redwood City.
"has again put on the Dumbarton cut off train": the service had stopped for a time in 1912.
No. 512 and No. 503, the "Redwood Mixed", daily except Sunday.
Still the Redwood Mixed on May 28, 1916.
"The Dumbarton train no longer carries passengers" under the timetable of Sunday, October 1, 1916.
Only freight trains over the bridge from October 1, 1916.

lines.notes: Ends with the timetable of October 1, 1916, which the Washington Press reported; the last day with passengers isn't stated, and no Railroad Commission order on it was found. In 1912 the trains stopped for a time and were back by September 21; when they stopped isn't sourced. By 1914, one mixed train each way, Nos. 512 and 503.
